slides.headline: 1. You forget why you walked into a room
slides.body: The doorway effect - your memory dumps context on every threshold. Untrained brains do this 40 times a day. Trained brains: 6-8.

slides.headline: 2. Reading same paragraph three times
slides.body: Attentional shift fires every 90 seconds by default. Without training, you re-read without noticing. With training, you catch the drift.

slides.headline: 3. Names vanish in 5 seconds after intro
slides.body: Working memory holds 4 items max under stress. Untrained brains lose the fifth as soon as it lands.

slides.headline: 4. You reach for phone before your feet touch floor
slides.body: First dopamine hit before cortisol clears. Sets low-attention baseline for 4 to 6 hours after.

slides.headline: 5. Cannot finish an article without checking notifications
slides.body: Split attention halves comprehension. Study Stanford 2024 - 47 percent recall drop with second screen.

caption:
7 signs your brain is on the wrong autopilot. Save this before you scroll on.

Most focus problems are not about willpower. They are default settings your brain runs when it has not been trained recently. The seven signs on the slides are the most reliable markers - if three or more feel familiar, the drill on slide 8 fixes them in about 10 minutes a day for 30 days. Comment FOCUS and I will send the exact exercises Cambridge researchers used in the 2026 study.
